parsed.notes: Lens B only; no support or quote-fidelity defects were raised.

reasons: Lake record status is verified and identity matches Smith v. Maryland, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1979-06-20.
Lake citations include official cite 442 U.S. 735, parallel cites 99 S. Ct. 2577 and 61 L. Ed. 2d 220, and vendor-neutral cite 1979 U.S. LEXIS 134.
Lake treatment field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, so the authority is treated as live under the disclosed record.
residual_risks: Treatment edges include proposed negative classifications, but none is final or tied to a point override in the disclosed lake record.

reasons: Lens B does not adjudicate whether the home-role label is substantively optimal.
No disclosed final treatment limitation makes Smith stale for a Third-Party Doctrine & CSLI home; lake scope_note calls it a foundational third-party-doctrine case and says it remains good law.
residual_risks: Role strength is a support/content-organization question reserved to Lens A.

reasons: Lens B does not test holding support or quote fidelity.
For currency only, the lake treatment fields mark Smith good_law as of 2026-06-30 and list no point_overrides limiting the pen-register holding.
residual_risks: Holding accuracy and quotation support are outside this lens.

defect.locator_note: lake.treatment.derivation and lake.treatment.edges; proposed negative edges are not final point_overrides.
defect.problem: The good-law call survives because lake.treatment itself says good_law and the scope_note says Smith remains good law, but the same disclosed treatment record contains unresolved proposed negative progeny/audit flags. The page should not present the treatment as completely clean without preserving that audit caveat internally.
defect.proposed_fix: Retain good_law only with an audit qualifier or complete the treatment audit resolving the proposed negative edges, especially the Carpenter edge, before treating this as a clean as-of-2026 call.

reasons: Lake treatment matches the page: field_i_validity is good_law, as_of_treatment is 2026-06-30, varies_by_point is false, and point_overrides is empty.

Lake scope_note states: Foundational third-party-doctrine case; remains good law. Carpenter v. United States (2018) declined to extend the third-party doctrine to cell-site location information but expressly did not overrule Smith.

Adversarial caveat: treatment.derivation shows audit_needed true, and treatment.edges include proposed negative labels, including Carpenter labeled overruled, so the disclosed record is not fully clean.
residual_risks: The Carpenter full text is not in the disclosed files; the 'expressly did not overrule' statement is accepted from the lake treatment judgment.
All negative edges reviewed here are marked proposed, so they do not independently overrule the lake good_law field.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add an internal treatment-audit note or resolve proposed negative edges before publishing the status as an unqualified clean treatment call.

reasons: Lake identity lists court as U.S. Supreme Court, court_id scotus, and court_level scotus.
The page authority_weight Binding — SCOTUS is consistent with that disclosed court identity.
No disclosed final treatment limitation changes the court-weight label.
